title: Bar chart
description:
A bar chart shows one value per category: `x_column` names the bars, `y_column` (or
`y_columns`, or `series_column` for long data) gives their lengths. Horizontal by
default; `renderer: vertical` draws columns. See `:help dbdash-chart-types`.

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: horizontal (default): color, show_values
show.description:
Horizontal bars, one line each, the value after the bar (`show_values`, default on);
`style.color` colors every bar (CSS `color`).

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: renderer: vertical
show.description:
`renderer: vertical` draws columns with ⅛-cell tops, the value above each. Try it on
any bar chart with `:DbDashStyle bar vertical`.

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: y_columns: grouped (side by side)
show.description:
Several `y_columns` draw one bar per series in each category, side by side (Chart.js
grouped bars, the default `style.group`), with a legend.

query.sql:
SELECT q AS quarter, r AS region, 100 + abs(random() % 200) AS sales
FROM (SELECT 'Q1' AS q UNION ALL SELECT 'Q2' UNION ALL SELECT 'Q3' UNION ALL SELECT 'Q4'),
     (SELECT 'EU' AS r UNION ALL SELECT 'US' UNION ALL SELECT 'APAC')

show.title: series_column, group: stacked
show.description:
Long data (one row per quarter and region) with `series_column`, stacked
(`style.group: stacked`, Chart.js `stacked: true`): the column is the total, the
value above it too. `palette: tableau` colors the regions.

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: sort: desc, top: 4, value_position: inside
show.description:
`sort` orders the bars by value (`asc` / `desc`; the total when stacked), `top` keeps
the first N (ECharts `dataZoom` without the zoom), `value_position: inside` writes the
value inside the end of the bar (ECharts `label.position: insideRight`).

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: bar_width, bar_gap
show.description:
`bar_width` is the columns per bar and `bar_gap` the columns between categories
(Chart.js `barThickness`, `categoryPercentage`); horizontal bars take them in lines.

query.sql:
SELECT 'Electronics' AS category, 920 AS sales, 1100 AS target
UNION ALL SELECT 'Clothing', 610, 500 UNION ALL SELECT 'Books', 240, 300
UNION ALL SELECT 'Home', 480, 450 UNION ALL SELECT 'Sports', 350, 400
UNION ALL SELECT 'Food', 700, 650

show.title: mark_lines, axes.y_axis: min_value, max_value
show.description:
Reference lines on the value axis (ECharts `markLine`): a goal and the `mean`. The
value axis runs from `min_value` to `max_value` (the bars' baseline and end).

query.sql:
SELECT 'Mon' AS day, 12 AS delta UNION ALL SELECT 'Tue', -8 UNION ALL SELECT 'Wed', 5
UNION ALL SELECT 'Thu', -3 UNION ALL SELECT 'Fri', 9

show.title: negative values, axes.y_axis.format
show.description:
Negative values grow left from zero; `axes.y_axis.format` is the Python format of the
value labels (`"{:+d}"` would show the sign; text around the field is kept).
